faqs.q: Should I buy one size bigger for an oversized T-shirt?
faqs.a: Usually not. A T-shirt sold as oversized is already cut wider, with dropped shoulders and a longer body, so most men should pick their normal size. Simply sizing up a regular T-shirt tends to make the sleeves and length too long and looks baggy rather than deliberately oversized. Check the brand's size chart for chest and length before buying.

faqs.q: Can short or slim men wear oversized T-shirts?
faqs.a: Yes. The key is balance: pair the loose tee with straight or slightly tapered bottoms rather than very wide ones, and choose a length that ends around the hips instead of mid-thigh. A half tuck at the front also helps show your waist so the outfit does not swallow your frame.

faqs.q: Should you tuck in an oversized T-shirt?
faqs.a: Oversized T-shirts are mostly worn untucked, as the relaxed drape is the point of the look. A loose front tuck can work well with cargos, wide-leg jeans or trousers, because it adds some shape at the waist. A full tuck usually looks bulky, since there is a lot of extra fabric.

faqs.q: Which fabric is best for an oversized T-shirt in Indian summers?
faqs.a: Breathable cotton is the most comfortable choice for hot and humid weather. Thicker, heavyweight cotton holds the boxy oversized shape better and suits cooler months or air-conditioned spaces, while lighter cotton or cotton-linen blends feel cooler in peak summer. Lighter colours also stay cooler in the sun than black.
